Method getValue simply delegates to delegate.getValue(index). So exceptions can come from delegate: NullPointerException if delegate is null, IllegalArgumentException if delegate rejects index, maybe UnsupportedOperationException if delegate doesn't support getValue, maybe IndexOutOfBoundsException (already covered). Also possible scenario: delegate is null leading to NullPointerException. Also scenario: delegate throws checked exception? Not likely because getValue signature doesn't declare throws. So only unchecked.

Also scenario: delegate returns null (already covered). Maybe delegate returns a Num that is null? Already covered.

Also scenario: delegate throws ArithmeticException (e.g., division by zero inside delegate). So test case: delegate that throws ArithmeticException for certain index.

Also scenario: delegate throws IllegalStateException (e.g., not initialized). Add that.
